recent_posts.title: How to test APIs with visual flows and CI automation
recent_posts.summary: A frontend developer shares how to improve API testing workflows beyond manual UI clicking or raw curl commands. Using a sponsored tool called DevTools, you can record browser network requests, export them as HAR files, and import them into visual API flows that can be replayed, modified, and extended with conditional logic. These flows can also be exported to YAML and run in CI pipelines for automated testing, removing the need for manual checks after each code push.

recent_posts.title: How an agentic AI workflow helped ship 100 PRs in one month
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares their experience using an agentic AI workflow (the 'Ralph approach') with Claude to build a JavaScript game using Phaser. Over one month, they completed 100 significant PRs — far more than would have been possible manually. The workflow uses a manager Claude instance to plan features broken into phases, which are then executed sequentially by spawned Ralph agents. Each agent handles one phase, writes to a shared memory file, and terminates to let the next agent continue. Quality gates (TypeScript compilation, tests) are enforced at the end of each track. The developer reports clean, well-architected code output with rare regressions, needing to intervene in under 10% of cases. They attribute the strong results partly to JavaScript being well-represented in LLM training data, Phaser's code-only approach, and starting from a well-structured codebase.

recent_posts.title: Using git worktree to work alongside AI agents
recent_posts.summary: Git worktrees enable multiple branches to be checked out simultaneously on the same filesystem, solving the problem of context switching and AI agent workflows. When AI agents work on tasks that take significant time, worktrees allow developers to continue working on the main codebase independently. The feature creates a separate copy of the project elsewhere on your filesystem while sharing the same git tracking, making it possible to work on different branches concurrently without conflicts.

recent_posts.title: Using LLMs to optimize JavaScript performance in game development
recent_posts.summary: Using LLMs to optimize JavaScript performance has proven highly effective across 20+ real-world scenarios, reducing turnaround time from hours or days to minutes. The approach involves profiling with DevTools to identify bottlenecks, then having AI analyze and fix the code. Results include transforming a game from 20-30 FPS to near 60 FPS even with 4x CPU slowdown. LLMs successfully handled everything from simple closure optimizations to advanced techniques like baking tile maps into static textures and implementing complex bit-shifting algorithms. While some knowledge transfer is sacrificed, the speed and reliability of AI-driven solutions make them practical for shipping projects without accumulating technical debt.

recent_posts.title: Managing AI coding tools through disciplined refactoring and architectural control
recent_posts.summary: A frontend engineer shares insights from building a JavaScript survival game over one year, revealing how AI coding tools can provide 5-10x productivity gains when properly managed. The key is balancing rapid AI-assisted feature development with disciplined refactoring to maintain code structure. AI excels at self-contained, black-box tasks like algorithms and shaders, but developers must carefully manage system architecture and data flows. Frontend developers' experience with state management and modular architecture positions them well to leverage AI effectively while avoiding technical debt accumulation.

top_posts.title: Boosting game performance with web workers in Angular
top_posts.summary: Using web workers in Angular with Phaser can drastically improve performance by offloading computationally expensive tasks like the wave function collapse algorithm from the main thread. This allows the game to render terrain without causing freezing or requiring loading screens. Web workers handle the heavy computations and communicate results back to the main thread, ensuring smooth gameplay and responsive UI.

top_posts.title: I actually use JavaScript generator functions
top_posts.summary: Generator functions in JavaScript, though underutilized, are powerful tools for creating iterable sequences. This post explores their use in Motion Canvas, a library for creating animated presentations. By leveraging generators, Motion Canvas allows control over animations' timing, making scene development intuitive and flexible. The post provides a basic implementation example to understand this mechanism.

top_posts.title: Why I'm still using RxJS (not signals) for host binding in Angular
top_posts.summary: The post explores the use of RxJS for host binding in Angular as opposed to signals. The author shares personal insights and preferences, highlighting that while signals can be useful, RxJS offers more benefits in terms of code readability and maintainability. The discussion includes an example of a game component with keyboard event handling using both approaches.

top_posts.title: Profiling for high performance JavaScript applications
top_posts.summary: The post details how the author used browser profiling tools to identify and fix performance issues in a JavaScript game. Techniques discussed include identifying slow frames, spotting memory leaks, and using flame graphs to trace problematic code. By spreading update actions over multiple frames and cleaning up particle emitter references, significant performance improvements were achieved.
